promise_band.headline: Full Cleanup On Every Job
promise_band.body: Ask around Miami-Dade about tree crews and you will hear the same complaint: the tree came down and the debris stayed up. We bring our own chipper and chip truck to every job, so branches are chipped as we cut and everything leaves with us the same day. Driveways, walkways and pool decks are blown clean before we go. That is not an add-on line on the invoice — it is part of the price you were quoted.

signature_system.headline: The Owner Quotes It, The Crew Does It
signature_system.intro: Tropical South is a working tree service, not a call centre with subcontractors. Rafael prices the job on site, the same crew turns up to do it, and the number you were given is the number you pay.

blocks.title: We handle the county permits
blocks.body: Miami-Dade requires a permit to remove protected and heritage species, and Coral Gables and Pinecrest administer their own on top of the county's. Getting that wrong carries real fines and mandatory replanting. We identify what is protected during the quote, tell you plainly what applies, and coordinate the paperwork — including a written assessment through our ISA certified arborist partners where the application needs one.

blocks.title: Equipment that reaches the tree
blocks.body: Bucket lift for street-side work, tracked spider lift for back gardens and narrow side returns, chipper and chip truck on every job. The spider lift fits through a standard side gate and spreads its weight across turf, which is how we reach trees behind the house without putting a truck on your lawn or telling you it cannot be done.

seo_body.headline: Tree Removal, Trimming And Stump Grinding In Miami-Dade County
paragraphs: South Florida grows trees twelve months a year, which is why a canopy that cleared your roof last spring is into the tiles by this one. Live oak, ficus, mahogany, black olive and royal palm all put on serious growth here, and the maintenance window that keeps them safe is much shorter than most homeowners expect.

Then there is 1 June to 30 November. The trees that fail in a Miami-Dade hurricane are rarely the sickly ones — they are the big, dense, healthy-looking specimens whose canopies have never been thinned, and the ones carrying deadwood nobody has looked at from thirty feet up. Miami-Dade County's own guidance is to prune ahead of the season rather than during it, and once a storm is named every crew in the county is committed.

We handle all of it from one number: the routine trimming and stump grinding, the removals and the permits that go with them, the 24/7 storm response when something comes down at 2am, and the ISA-certified arborist reports when the county, an insurer or an HOA board wants it in writing.

Trimming, crown reduction and canopy thinning to ISA standards
Stump grinding below grade, ready to replant or sod
Miami-Dade DERM and city permit coordination

faqs.q: How much does tree removal cost in Miami-Dade County?
faqs.a: Removals generally run from $250 to $3,500 or more, depending on the size of the tree, how close it is to structures, how hazardous it is and whether equipment can reach it. Trimming and pruning is typically $150 to $950 per tree, and stump grinding $100 to $450 per stump. Every quote is free and given in writing before any work starts.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Miami-Dade?
faqs.a: For protected and heritage species, yes. Miami-Dade County DERM administers the tree ordinance countywide, and Coral Gables and Pinecrest run their own permitting on top of it. Fines for unpermitted removal are significant and replacement planting is often mandatory. We identify what is protected at the quote and coordinate the permit for you.

faqs.q: Do you offer emergency tree service?
faqs.a: Yes — 24/7 across Miami-Dade for storm damage, fallen trees and hazardous situations. Call (305) 299-1189 and Rafael responds personally. Our normal hours for quotes and scheduled work are 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM, Monday to Saturday.

faqs.q: Is cleanup included, or is it extra?
faqs.a: Included, on every job. We bring our own chipper and chip truck, so branches are chipped as we cut and everything is hauled away the same day. Driveways, walkways and pool decks are blown clean before we leave.

faqs.q: How quickly can you give me a quote?
faqs.a: Usually the same day you call. Rafael walks the property himself, prices the work and gives you a written scope at no charge and with no obligation.

Yes, fully licensed and insured in Miami-Dade County, and we have been operating since 2019. That matters most when the work is happening directly over your roof, your pool cage or a neighbour's property.

faqs.q: When should I trim my trees for hurricane season?
faqs.a: Before it starts. Season runs 1 June to 30 November, and Miami-Dade County advises pruning ahead of it rather than during it. The useful booking window is late winter and spring — once a storm is named, every tree crew in the county is committed.

faqs.q: Do you top trees or do 'hurricane cuts'?
faqs.a: No. Topping destroys a tree's structure and forces weak regrowth that is more likely to fail in the next storm, and the county's own guidance tells homeowners not to allow it. We thin and reduce to ISA standards instead, and we will explain the difference on site.

faqs.q: What trees do you work on?
faqs.a: Every species common to South Florida — royal and coconut palms, queen palms, live oak, mango, avocado, gumbo limbo, ficus, black olive, mahogany and more. Palms and hardwoods are handled very differently and the crew is equipped for both.

faqs.q: Do you work with HOAs and commercial properties?
faqs.a: Yes. We run scheduled maintenance contracts for HOA communities, property managers and commercial owners across Miami-Dade, including pre-season storm prep and priority response after a named storm.
